text:
Alex: heads-up, saw cross-namespace KMS decrypts in a customer's private cluster during a vuln scan :eyes:
Priya: link?
Alex: redacted link to audit bucket, but summary: decrypt calls from namespace `tenant-b` against key owned by `tenant-a` — SA looks like `injection-worker`
Maria: yikes. do we have any clusterrole bindings for that SA?
Alex: running quick check now, but initial `kubectl get rolebinding,clusterrolebinding --all-namespaces | grep injection-worker` shows a clusterrolebinding that looks out of scope
Sam: could be two causes: mis-scoped RBAC OR a network/agent that proxies keystore requests across namespaces
Luca: also check node-mounted keystore socket. onprem package had a daemon that mounts /var/run/keystore to host. if pods can access hostpath that could bypass k8s boundaries
Priya: immediate mitigations: 1) add deny-all egress netpol for tenant-b except to keystore-proxy svc, 2) remove any clusterrolebinding for that SA, 3) rotate affected keys and audit retentions
Alex: netpol snippet I tested locally: ```apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-except-keystore
  namespace: tenant-b
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: ["Egress"]
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: keystore-proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
Sam: good. also check for any Service of type ExternalName or headless svc that could be abused for DNS-based egress
Maria: audit logging question: what's current decrypt log retention for private customers? can we bump short-term to 90d for this tenant while we triage?
Priya: we can change retention in the agent config; I'll file a quick ticket to increase to 90d and enable alerting on cross-namespace decrypts
Alex: alert idea: rule that flags decrypts where `requesting_namespace != key_owner_namespace` and fires to sec-oncall
Luca: RBAC fix: create a policy to reject ClusterRoleBindings that reference tenant-scoped SAs automatically in admission (validating webhook). short-term remove the offending binding
Sam: will also verify no hostPath mounts expose keystore socket: `kubectl get pods -A -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace} {.spec.volumes[*].hostPath.path}{"
"}{end}' | grep /var/run/keystore`
Alex: I've rotated keys for tenant-a and revoked the short-lived tokens for service accounts in tenant-b :rotating_light:
Maria: assign owners — Priya owns retention/alerts, Sam owns immediate host/net checks, Luca owns admission policy proposal, Alex continues triage and key rotation. please update the incident doc
Priya: filing incident doc and adding run steps now. will notify customer with a measured statement (no evidence of exfil yet) :speech_balloon:
deploy-bot: Incident ticket INC-2026 created by Priya — assign/labels: "onprem","kms","investigation"
Alex: thanks. next steps: confirm clusterrolebinding removal and netpol applied, then validate audit logs for any unexplained decrypts older than 7d
Sam: will post results in this thread in ~30m
Maria: good. if anyone sees further decrypts after controls, escalate to incident ops and consider tenant isolation (node/pool eviction) :hammer:
Priya: noted. adding checklist: [1] revoke offending SA tokens, [2] remove clusterrolebinding, [3] apply netpol lockdown, [4] rotate keys, [5] increase retention, [6] create alert rule
Alex: thanks team :thumbsup:
